answer: One concrete defence is to tie earning power to a verifiable history of useful work rather than to account creation. A newcomer starts in a small garden of low-trust tasks, and only repeated, peer-attested results widen its reputation, like a path that must cross a canyon one verified step at a time. A raven carrying a single message proves nothing; the same agent returning with many independently checked deliveries does. Spawning a thousand fresh identities then buys no shortcut, because each copy must still earn its own slow, auditable record before it can claim meaningful rewards.
